newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed, Intel falls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed, Intel falls.

text.p: U.S. stocks traded in London were mixed on Monday, gingerly awaiting Wall Street's open after Friday's volatility, traders said.

The Dow industrials closed at 8,194.04, down 29 points, after dropping more than 100 points. Robust U.S. employment and manufacturing data led to a sharp sell-off in the bond market, rattling investors.

Wall Street stocks were expected to open mixed to a bit softer. In GLOBEX trading at 1048 GMT, the September S&P futures contract fell 1.25 points to 951.75 and the September long bond contract rose 6/32 to 115.
"The comeback was incredible," one trader said. "I would expect it maybe be a little softer in the morning but the tech stocks may be a little bouncey."
Technology share interest was expected to pick up ahead of this week's Macworld Expo trade show in Boston.
Intel Corp stock fell 5/8 to $93 after Motorola Inc and IBM Corp said on Monday they would introduce three PowerPc microprocessors.
Motorola said the systems would challenge "Wintel", the alliance between Microsoft Corp's market-leading windows software and Intel Corp's processors.
Shares in Philip Morris fell 3/8 to $44-5/8.
The stock fell on signs the landmark billion-dollar passive smoking trial in Miami may not end soon, one trader said.
Jury selection for the suit began on June 2, six years after it was filed, and it went to trial on Friday.
In other activity, General Motors shares rose 1/8 to $64-9/16 and Pfizer Inc lost 1/4 from its Friday close of $58-11/16.
U.S. debt market players said they would focus on the Treasury's refunding this week.
The Treasury will sell $16 billion in three-year notes, $12 billion in 10-year notes and $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
